evidence.text: Conveys trusting (信) what a person (人) says (言).

Phono-semantic compound (形聲 /形声, OC *hljins): phonetic 人 (OC *njin) + semantic 言 (“words”). Shuowen interprets it as an ideogrammic compound.
Schuessler (2007) reconstructs the Old Chinese minimally as *sin and suggests possible derivation from 允 (OC *winʔ, “to trust; to be true”).
Alternatively, Sagart and Baxter (2012) reconstruct *s-niŋ-s (*s-ni[ŋ]-s in Baxter and Sagart, 2014) and suggest a derivation from 仁 (OC *niŋ, “kind”) with the prefix *s-, probably used to increase its valency.

evidence.source: CUHK Humanum 漢語多功能字庫
evidence.text: Warring States bronze forms combine 人 with 言; variants replace 人 with 身. The similar sounds of 人 and 身 support their phonetic function. The semantic interpretation is trustworthy human speech; original meaning sincerity.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 信
